name: Scaffold
desc: A tube-and-clamp scaffold standing in perspective — standards, ledgers, transoms and facade braces lacing an open steel lattice across two rows, boards decking each lift, torn debris netting breathing on the outer face and a hoist load creeping the elevation.

energy.doc: sun catch on the tubes, netting breath and camera parallax

scale.doc: lift height, tube girth and row spacing (2.2 = a heavy rig that crowds the frame; the bay width stays fixed so this is never a no-op)

density.doc: bays across and lifts up (3x2 to 6x5)

speed.doc: rate the sun crawls the facade and the hoist creeps; the camera keeps breathing regardless so it never goes static

hue.doc: sun/netting hue; the steel takes its complement

netting.doc: how much debris netting is hung — it is translucent, so 1 veils the bg rather than hiding it

style.doc: aesthetic: cold galvanised steel / oxidised decay / form from light alone / cyan schematic linework / hatched paper plate

seed.doc: which bays are braced and netted, board wear, tube weathering

alpha.doc: layer opacity — scales every mark, so it dissolves into the background instead of veiling it
